Let the measure of the unknown interior angle of the given triangle be [MATH: y{:}]

In any triangle, the sum of the measures of the interior angles is always [MATH: 180^\circ.] So, in the given triangle, we have

[MATH: 45^{∘} + 43^{∘} + y|= 180^{∘}; 88^{∘} + y|= 180^{∘}; y|= 180^{∘} − 88^{∘}; y|= 92^{∘}.]

[MATH: x + y|= 180^{∘}; x + 92^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x|= 180^{∘} − 92^{∘}; x|= 88^{∘}.]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: x] is [MATH: 88^\circ.]

[MATH: x^{∘} + z^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x^{∘} + 77^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x^{∘}|= 103^{∘}.]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: x] is [MATH: 103.]
